script: Hey everyone, welcome to "Chillwave B2".
I'm Ethan.
Tonight, I thought we’d chat about something a little fun — and practical: traveling on a budget.
I just closed my laptop after looking up cheap flights, and let me tell you, I learned a few things.
So, kick back, maybe grab a snack, and let’s see if we can make your next trip a little more affordable.
A few years back, I took a bus to a small town in Colorado for a music festival.
We crashed on a friend’s couch to skip hotel costs and split a big pot of spaghetti for dinner.
Most of the shows were free, but the highlight was a secret concert in some guy’s backyard.
We hiked to scenic spots instead of paying for tours and just brought a blanket for picnics.
Heh, I remember laughing when we realized we’d spent less than $200 for the whole trip.
What’s the cheapest way you’ve ever seen someone travel?
I did this road trip thing a while back with a buddy who swore by the "spare tire" budget method.
He packed snacks like someone planning a military campaign — granola bars, peanut butter, the whole nine yards.
We camped in national forests instead of booking a hotel, which saved a bunch and let us actually sleep under the stars.
We listened to podcasts the whole way, called it our "free entertainment pass."
Heh, and we even got free drinks at gas stations by asking the attendants — turns out they’re pretty friendly after midnight.
Ever tried turning a car into your base camp instead of checking into a place?"
So, what’s your plan when it comes to cheap adventures?
Maybe you’ve got a trick up your sleeve that I haven’t tried yet.
Would you skip meals to save money or go for free roadside snacks?
Heh, I’m curious if people actually enjoy sleeping in cars or if it’s pure stubbornness.
Let me know where you’d go if you had to keep the costs low but the memories high.
We’ll be back in a little bit with some music to help you figure it out.

Alright, here’s a little tip I picked up from some clever travelers — sometimes the best way to save cash is to go off-season. Like, if you wanna visit the beach, maybe skip July and hit it up in April. You’ll get fewer crowds and way better deals. A phrase that comes to mind here is “the best time to plant a tree was 10 years ago; the second-best time is now.” Heh, it’s kind of true for trips too — just maybe not during peak prices. So, what’s a place you’d go out of season for a cheaper thrill? Let me know — I’m all ears.

Alright, that's all for tonight's ramble on road trips and rice snack bars. Maybe the best part of traveling cheap is figuring out what really matters — like friends, free music, or a good blanket. Thanks for hanging out and letting me share this weird little corner of the world with you. Take care, and remember, sometimes low cost just means higher fun.
